chunks: Al-Kafi: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There was a woman in Madinah who used to be approached [by men], so this news reached Umar, so he sent for her and frightened her, and ordered that she be brought to him. The woman became terrified, and labor seized her, so she went to one of the houses and gave birth to a boy. The boy cried out (istahala), then he died. So it entered into his [Umar's] heart, due to Allah's will, [the weight of] the woman's fright and the death of the boy. Some of his companions said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, you are not accountable for this.' And some of them said: 'What is this?' [implying it is insignificant]. He said: 'Ask Abu al-Hasan.' So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to them: 'If you have exercised Ijtihad, you have not hit the mark; and if you have spoken based on your personal opinion, you have indeed erred.' Then he said: 'Upon you is the blood-money (diyah) of the child.'

key_terms.اسْتَهَلَ: To cry out loudly immediately after birth

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the blood-money for a child born prematurely due to fright caused by a ruler?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the application of *Diyyat al-Haml* (blood-money for the fetus) in the context of Umar ibn al-Adh's administration, highlighting the juristic debate between *Ijtihad* (independent reasoning) and *Ra'y* (personal opinion). Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that while the companions' reasoning was not entirely baseless, it was technically incorrect, thereby establishing the precedent that the father is liable for the fetus's blood-money upon its death due to external trauma. This incident serves as a foundational case study in Shia fiqh for determining compensation in cases of accidental fetal loss.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/-] al-Kafi: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Asimi from Ali b. al-Hasan al-Maythami from Ali b. Asbat from his paternal uncle Ya`qub b. Salim from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام who said:

there was a woman in Madina who used to be approached by men [she was a prostitute], this news reached Umar so he sent for her and frightened her and ordered that she be brought to him, so the woman became terrified and started getting contractions, she fled to one of the houses and gave premature birth to a boy, the boy cried out loud and then died, so it entered in his (Umar’s) heart what Allah wished to enter because of his frightening of the woman and the death of the boy, some of his sitting companions said to him: O commander of the faithful you don’t have to do anything because of this, while others said: what is this? [belittling it – as if to say it is nothing], he said: ask Aba al-Hasan, so Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام said to them: if you have done Ijtihad then you have not got it right, and if you have said it based on your personal opinion then you have made a mistake, then he said: upon you is to give the blood-money of the child.
